title: Enforcement Decree of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Formulation of Master Plans)
(1) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety intends to amend a master plan for the promotion of the disaster and safety industry formulated pursuant to Article 5(1) of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") (hereinafter referred to as a "master plan"), the Minister shall do so following deliberation by the Central Safety Management Committee under Article 9 of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety.
(2) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety has formulated or amended a master plan, the Minister shall notify the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments thereof and make a public announcement thereof on the website of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.

Article 3 (Formulation of Implementation Plans)
(1) An implementation plan under Article 6(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan") shall include the following matters:
1. Results of implementation in the preceding year;
2. The direction for project implementation for the relevant year;
3. Detailed implementation plans by sector;
4. Support plans for each major project;
5. Other matters necessary for the promotion of the disaster and safety industry.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may request the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments to submit materials or opinions necessary for the formulation or amendment of an implementation plan. In such cases, a person receiving a request shall cooperate unless there is a special reason for not doing so.
(3) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety has formulated or amended an implementation plan, the Minister shall notify the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies and the heads of local governments thereof and make a public announcement thereof on the website of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.

Article 4 (Establishment of a Classification System for the Disaster and Safety Industry)
When establishing or supplementing a classification system for the disaster and safety industry under Article 7 of the Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall take into consideration international trends, the emergence of new technologies, and the like in the field of the disaster and safety industry.

Article 5 (Fact-Finding Surveys on the Disaster and Safety Industry)
(1) A fact-finding survey on the disaster and safety industry under Article 8(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "fact-finding survey") shall cover the following matters:
1. General conditions, such as the number of businesses related to the disaster and safety industry in Korea, their sales, and the numbers of persons engaged in such businesses;
2. The status of commercialization of disaster and safety technologies or related research and development;
3. Trends in the entry of domestic disaster and safety business operators into overseas disaster and safety industry markets;
4. Other matters for which the Minister of the Interior and Safety deems a fact-finding survey necessary to develop policies for fostering the disaster and safety industry.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall conduct a fact-finding survey once each year. In such cases, the Minister shall prepare a survey plan that includes the purpose, content, period, etc. of the fact-finding survey and notify the persons subject to the survey in advance.
(3) Where necessary to conduct a fact-finding survey efficiently, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may conduct the survey using information and communications networks or electronic methods such as electronic mail.

Article 6 (Operation of the Comprehensive Information System)
Where necessary for the efficient management of information on the disaster and safety industry, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may operate the comprehensive information system under Article 9(2) of the Act by linking it with public and private information systems.

Article 7 (Designation and Revocation of Designation, etc. of Institutions for Training Professionals in the Disaster and Safety Industry)
(1) An institution for training professionals in the disaster and safety industry under Article 10(2) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "training institution") may provide education and training on the following matters:
1. Understanding of the disaster and safety industry;
2. Commercialization of disaster and safety technologies and disaster and safety products;
3. Development of disaster and safety-related services;
4. Other matters that the Minister of the Interior and Safety or the head of a local government deems necessary for the promotion of the disaster and safety industry.
(2) The criteria for designation of a training institution under Article 10(2) of the Act shall be as follows. Provided, That a local government may prescribe different criteria for designation of training institutions by ordinance of that local government, taking into consideration the conditions of the relevant region.
1. The institution shall have formulated a plan for providing the education and training under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as "education and training" in this paragraph);
2. The institution shall have the educational facilities and educational equipment necessary for education and training;
3. The institution shall have secured professional teaching personnel and dedicated operating personnel necessary for education and training;
4. The institution shall have formulated a plan for securing the operating funds necessary for the operation of the training institution;
5. The institution shall meet the criteria prescribed by public notice by the Minister of the Interior and Safety in addition to the matters prescribed in subparagraphs 1 through 4.
(3) A person intending to be designated as a training institution pursuant to Article 10(2) of the Act shall apply for designation to the Minister of the Interior and Safety or the head of a local government, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.
(4) Where a person applying for designation pursuant to paragraph (3) meets the criteria for designation under paragraph (2), the Minister of the Interior and Safety or the head of a local government shall issue a certificate of designation as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety and make a public announcement of the designation on the website of the relevant institution.
(5) The detailed criteria for revocation of the designation of a training institution under Article 10(4) of the Act shall be as specified in the attached Table.
(6) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (5), matters necessary for the designation and revocation of designation of training institutions shall be determined and prescribed by public notice by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.

Article 8 (Support for Costs)
The Minister of the Interior and Safety or the head of a local government may, pursuant to Article 10(3) of the Act and within the limits of the budget, provide training institutions with support for all or part of the following costs:
1. Costs necessary for operating educational programs, such as lecture fees and personnel expenses;
2. Costs necessary for developing and distributing educational materials;
3. Costs necessary for renting training venues and purchasing equipment, such as equipment for practical training;
4. Costs necessary for surveys and research for the training of specialized personnel in the disaster and safety industry.

Article 9 (Designation and Operation of Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Facilities)
(1) The requirements for designation as a disaster and safety industry promotion facility under Article 13(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "promotion facility") shall be as follows: Provided, That a local government may prescribe different requirements for the designation of promotion facilities by its ordinance in consideration of the conditions in the relevant region.
1. At least 5 disaster and safety business operators shall occupy the facility for which designation as a promotion facility is sought (hereinafter in this paragraph referred to as the "subject facility");
2. At least 30/100 of the disaster and safety business operators occupying the subject facility shall be operators of small and medium enterprises under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises;
3. The area occupied by facilities used by disaster and safety business operators and their supporting facilities (including the facilities for common use under subparagraph 4) shall account for at least 50/100 of the total gross floor area of the subject facility;
4. Facilities for common use necessary for carrying out disaster and safety industry activities, such as common conference rooms and common equipment rooms, shall be installed;
5. Complementarity and links with existing promotion facilities and businesses and institutions related to the disaster and safety industry shall be secured;
6. An operational plan shall be prepared, including measures for organizational composition, financing, equipment use, facility management, etc.
(2) A person intending to obtain designation as a promotion facility pursuant to Article 13(1) of the Act shall apply for designation to the Minister of the Interior and Safety or the head of a local government, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, attaching documents proving that the requirements for designation under paragraph (1) are met.
(3) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety or the head of a local government designates a promotion facility, the Minister or head shall publicly announce that fact on the website of the relevant institution.
(4) The Minister of the Interior and Safety or the head of a local government may inspect the operational status of a promotion facility designated pursuant to Article 13(1) of the Act.
(5) Matters necessary for the designation and operation, etc. of promotion facilities, other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (4), shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety or by municipal ordinance.

Article 10 (Withdrawal of Designation of Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Facilities)
(1) Where a promotion facility ceases to meet the requirements for designation under Article 9(1), the Minister of the Interior and Safety or the head of a local government may set a period not exceeding 3 months and require that the requirements for designation be met. In such cases, the person required to meet the requirements for designation shall meet them within that period.
(2) The Minister of the Interior and Safety and the head of a local government shall, before withdrawing the designation of a promotion facility pursuant to Article 13(4) of the Act, hear the opinion of the head of the relevant local government in advance.
(3) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety or the head of a local government withdraws the designation of a promotion facility pursuant to Article 13(4) of the Act, the Minister or head shall publicly announce that fact on the website of the relevant institution.

Article 11 (Designation of Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Complexes)
In order to request the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, pursuant to Article 6(2) of the Industrial Sites and Development Act, to designate a disaster and safety industry promotion complex under Article 13(1) of the Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may gather opinions from local governments or institutions, corporations, organizations, etc. related to the disaster and safety industry.

Article 12 (Criteria and Procedures for Designation of New Technology, Etc.)
(1) New disaster and safety technology under Article 14(1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "new technology") shall comply with disaster and safety-related statutes and regulations, and the criteria for its designation shall be as follows:
1. Novelty: Technologies in the disaster and safety field and related technologies that have been developed for the first time in Korea or have innovatively improved or refined major parts of domestic or foreign technologies;
2. Excellence of technical performance: Technologies possessing efficiency, completeness, significance, and potential for development.
(2) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety receives an application for designation of new technology pursuant to Article 14(3) of the Act, the Minister shall examine the application in accordance with the designation criteria under paragraph (1) and decide whether to grant designation within 90 days from the date of application. In such cases, periods prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety shall not be included in the examination period.
(3) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety deems it necessary for the examination under paragraph (2), the Minister shall hear the opinions of interested parties and specialized institutions in the relevant field.
(4) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety intends to hear the opinions of interested parties pursuant to paragraph (3), the Minister shall publicly announce the main details of the relevant technology for at least 30 days on an information and communications network designated by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.
(5) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety receives an application for an extension of the validity period of new technology designation pursuant to Article 14(3) of the Act, the Minister shall examine the following matters and decide whether to grant an extension. In such cases, the validity period may be extended to a maximum of 12 years, including the validity period for which designation was initially granted.
1. The extent to which the technology is recognized as superior to domestic and foreign technologies of the same type (same kind), in terms of its degree of technological advancement, disaster prevention effects, economic efficiency, safety, etc.;
2. The track record of utilization and the efforts made to disseminate the technology from the time of designation as new technology until the application for an extension of the validity period.
(6) Examinations under paragraphs (2) and (5) shall be conducted by means of on-site investigation (meaning verification of whether the details of the technology, its applicability on site, etc. correspond to the contents of the application for new technology designation or an extension of the validity period) and document review.
(7) A person who has obtained new technology designation pursuant to Article 14(4) of the Act may use a new technology mark prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety on facilities installed using the new technology, on products using it, or on their packaging, promotional materials, etc.
(8) A person who has obtained new technology designation pursuant to Article 14(4) of the Act shall prepare a record of utilization of the new technology, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety, and submit it to the Minister of the Interior and Safety each year.
(9) Matters necessary for new technology designation and extension of the validity period of new technology designation, etc., other than those provided for in paragraphs (1) through (8), shall be prescribed and publicly notified by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.

Article 13 (Procedures for Revocation of New Technology Designation)
Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety revokes new technology designation pursuant to Article 15(1) of the Act, the Minister shall publicly announce that fact on an information and communications network designated by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.

Article 14 (Products Eligible for Certification as Disaster and Safety Products and Certification Criteria)
(1) The products eligible for conformity certification of disaster and safety products under Article 16 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "certification") shall be as follows:
1. Disaster and safety products capable of protecting human life, the human body, or property from disasters or various other accidents;
2. Disaster and safety products that can be used for disaster prevention, preparedness, response, and recovery activities;
3. Other disaster and safety products whose use or utilization by the public can reduce damage caused by disasters or improve the level of safety management.
(2) The criteria for certification shall be as follows:
1. The product shall accurately perform its functions as a disaster and safety product in accordance with its design or intended use;
2. The efficiency, usability, ease of maintenance and management, and other characteristics of the disaster and safety product shall meet or exceed the levels determined by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.
(3) Detailed matters concerning products eligible for certification and certification criteria shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.

Article 15 (Certification Procedures, etc.)
(1) Upon receiving an application for certification or an extension of the validity period of certification pursuant to Article 16 (3) of the Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may request relevant institutions to conduct tests, inspections, and other assessments, or hear the opinions of experts in the relevant field, to verify the performance of the product.
(2) Where deemed necessary to grant certification or extend the validity period of certification, the Minister of the Interior and Safety shall hear the opinions of interested persons.
(3) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety intends to hear the opinions of interested persons pursuant to paragraph (2), the Minister shall publicly announce the principal details concerning the relevant disaster and safety product on an information and communications network designated by the Minister for at least 30 days.
(4) The Minister of the Interior and Safety shall review the opinions submitted pursuant to paragraph (1) and notify the applicant and interested persons of the results of their handling, the reasons therefor, and other relevant matters.
(5) A person who has obtained certification pursuant to Article 16 (4) of the Act may use the certification mark prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety on the relevant product, its packaging, promotional materials, and the like.
(6) Matters necessary for certification and extensions of the validity period of certification, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (5), shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.

Article 16 (Procedures for Revocation of Certification)
Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety revokes certification pursuant to Article 18 (1) of the Act, the Minister shall publicly announce that fact on an information and communications network designated by the Minister.

Article 17 (Support for Preferential Use of New Technology or Certified Products)
Where a disaster management agency under Article 3, subparagraph 5 of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety (hereinafter referred to as a "disaster management agency") intends to preferentially use new technology or certified products (meaning disaster and safety products certified pursuant to Article 16 (4) of the Act) pursuant to Article 19 of the Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may provide necessary support, such as holding consultation meetings and providing information.

Article 18 (Support for Start-ups and Commercialization)
(1) Pursuant to Article 20 (1) of the Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may provide the following support to persons establishing enterprises as defined in Article 2 of the Support for Small and Medium Enterprise Establishment Act in the disaster and safety industry:
1. Consulting on legal, tax, accounting, management, and other matters necessary for establishing an enterprise;
2. Provision of information on technologies, sales channels, locations, and other matters relating to enterprise establishment;
3. Provision of education relating to enterprise establishment and support for related costs;
4. Provision of space within promotion facilities for establishing enterprises;
5. Other support to create jobs and promote enterprise establishment in the disaster and safety industry.
(2) Pursuant to Article 20 (2) of the Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may provide the following support to small and medium enterprises in the disaster and safety industry (meaning small and medium enterprises under Article 2 of the Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises):
1. Support for costs necessary to obtain domestic and overseas quality certifications;
2. Support for resolving technical and management difficulties;
3. Funding for research and development and commercialization;
4. Other support necessary to promote the commercialization of disaster and safety technology and disaster and safety products.
(3) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety intends to provide support pursuant to paragraphs (1) and (2), the Minister shall publicly announce the support plan on an information and communications network designated by the Minister, and a person seeking support shall apply to the Minister as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.
(4) Matters necessary concerning the details and procedures of support, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3), shall be determined by the Minister of the Interior and Safety.

Article 19 (Survey and Disclosure of Demand in the Disaster and Safety Industry)
(1) Pursuant to Article 21 (1) of the Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may each year request the heads of the following institutions, corporations, or organizations to submit the demand for construction works or services using disaster and safety products or disaster and safety technology and investment management plans for the following year:
1. Disaster management agencies;
2. Public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
3. Government-funded research institutes under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Research Institutes and government-funded science and technology research institutes under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Science and Technology Research Institutes;
4. Local public corporations and local public agencies under the Local Public Enterprises Act.
(2) The head of an institution, corporation, or organization receiving a request under paragraph (1) shall submit the demand and investment management plan.
(3) The Minister of the Interior and Safety may compile and analyze the demand and investment management plans related to the disaster and safety industry submitted pursuant to paragraph (2) and disclose the results in the Official Gazette and on an information and communications network designated by the Minister.

Article 20 (Establishment of the Disaster and Safety Industry Association)
Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety grants permission for the establishment of the Disaster and Safety Industry Association under Article 22 of the Act, the Minister shall publicly announce the details on the website of the Ministry of the Interior and Safety.

Article 21 (Entrustment of Affairs)
(1) Pursuant to Article 26 of the Act, the Minister of the Interior and Safety may entrust the affairs specified in subparagraphs 1 through 9 of that Article to institutions, corporations, or organizations related to the disaster and safety industry that are recognized as possessing the organization, personnel, and expertise necessary to perform those affairs.
(2) Where the Minister of the Interior and Safety entrusts affairs pursuant to paragraph (1), the Minister shall publicly notify the entrusted institution, corporation, or organization and the details of the entrusted affairs.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 33198, January 3, 2023>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on January 5, 2023.

Article 2 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) The Enforcement Decree of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act is partially amended as follows:
Articles 46 through 52, 52-2, and 52-3 shall be deleted, respectively.
(2) The Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety is partially amended as follows:
Articles 81-2 and 81-3 shall be deleted, respectively.
Article 88 (2) and (3) shall be deleted, respectively; and in paragraphs (5) and (6) of that Article, "paragraph (2) or (4)" shall each be replaced by "paragraph (4)".
Attached Tables 2-3 and 2-4 shall be deleted, respectively.
(3) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party is partially amended as follows:
In Article 26 (1) 2 (e), "new disaster prevention technology designated and publicly notified under Article 61 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act" shall be replaced by "new disaster and safety technology designated under Article 14 of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act"; in subparagraph 3 (e) of that paragraph, "Article 61 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act" shall be replaced by "Article 14 of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act"; and in item (j) of that subparagraph, "Article 73-4 (1) of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety" shall be replaced by "Article 16 (1) of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act".
(4) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Contracts to Which a Local Government Is a Party is partially amended as follows:
In Article 20 (1) 10 (e), "new disaster prevention technology designated and publicly notified under Article 61 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act" shall be replaced by "new disaster and safety technology designated under Article 14 of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act".
In Article 22, subparagraph 11, "new disaster prevention technology designated and publicly notified under Article 61 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act" shall be replaced by "new disaster and safety technology designated under Article 14 of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act".
In Article 25 (1) 4 (e), "new disaster prevention technology designated and publicly notified under Article 61 of the Countermeasures against Natural Disasters Act" shall be replaced by "new disaster and safety technology designated under Article 14 of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act"; subparagraph 6 (d) 4) (i) of that paragraph shall read as follows; and in 9) of that item, "Article 73-4 (1) of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety" shall be replaced by "Article 16 (1) of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act".
    (i) Article 14 of the Disaster and Safety Industry Promotion Act.
